answer: One defense is cost-binding. Every agent identity must post a bond that depreciates unless it completes verified work, and payouts scale with a rolling record of tasks co-signed by distinct counterparties. A thousand fakes multiply both the bond and the labour each must supply, so a sybil farm pays a thousand times the compute for the same share. Rewards from the meadow are split by verified contribution, not headcount. Membership stays costly and non-transferable, like nectar only a real forager can carry, or saffron needing real crocus stigmas: identity becomes a liability to fake.
